plan.title: Database Schema — All 17 SQLAlchemy Models + First Alembic Migration with RLS

task.description:
Create server/app/models/base.py — SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative base with common mixins.
Implementation: - DeclarativeBase with mapped_column defaults for common columns. - TimestampMixin: created_at (server_default=now()), updated_at (onupdate=now()). - UUIDPrimaryKeyMixin: id = mapped_column(UUID, primary_key=True, server_default=gen_random_uuid()). - UserOwnedMixin: user_id = mapped_column(UUID, ForeignKey("users.id"), nullable=False). - Import pgvector.sqlalchemy.Vector for embedding columns.
Create server/app/models/__init__.py — import all 17 model classes so Alembic autogenerate detects them.
task.verification: `from app.models.base import Base, TimestampMixin, UUIDPrimaryKeyMixin` imports without error. Base.metadata is accessible and collects all model tables after importing __init__.
task.done-condition: Base class uses SQLAlchemy 2.0 DeclarativeBase. Mixins provide id, created_at, updated_at, user_id columns. __init__.py imports all 17 model classes.

task.description:
Create all 17 SQLAlchemy model files. Each model in its own file under server/app/models/.
Models (table → file → key columns): 1. system_config → system_config.py: key (PK, String), value (JSONB), updated_at 2. users → user.py: id, username (unique), email, password_hash, role (enum: admin/user), display_name, title, vault_path, must_change_password (bool, default false), created_at, updated_at 3. sessions → session.py: id, user_id (FK), refresh_token_hash, device_info, ip_address, is_revoked (bool), expires_at, created_at 4. api_keys → api_key.py: id, user_id (FK, nullable — NULL=shared), provider, encrypted_key, key_type (personal/shared), label, created_at 5. documents → document.py: id, user_id (FK), namespace, title, file_path, content, content_hash, note_type, frontmatter (JSONB), word_count, indexed_at, created_at, updated_at 6. chunks → chunk.py: id, document_id (FK), user_id (FK), namespace, content, content_tsvector (generated, tsvector), embedding (Vector, nullable), chunk_index, enrichment_hash, token_count, created_at 7. wikilinks → wikilink.py: id, source_document_id (FK), target_document_id (FK, nullable), user_id (FK), namespace, target_title, alias, created_at 8. conversations → conversation.py: id, user_id (FK), project_id (FK, nullable), title, model_id, mode, mcp_mode (enum: disable/auto/manual, default disable), message_count, created_at, updated_at 9. messages → message.py: id, conversation_id (FK), user_id (FK), role (system/user/assistant/tool), content, model_id, token_count, citations (JSONB), tool_calls (JSONB), created_at 10. memories → memory.py: id, user_id (FK), content, embedding (Vector, nullable), memory_type, source_conversation_id (FK, nullable), importance, is_archived (bool), created_at, updated_at 11. dream_audit_log → dream_audit_log.py: id, user_id (FK), action, details (JSONB), memory_id (FK, nullable), created_at 12. projects → project.py: id, user_id (FK), name, description, include_folders (JSONB), exclude_folders (JSONB), tags (JSONB), system_prompt, default_model_id, created_at, updated_at 13. operation_log → operation_log.py: id, user_id (FK), operation_type, steps (JSONB), status (pending/applied/undone), created_at 14. llm_usage → llm_usage.py: id, user_id (FK), model, provider, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd (Numeric), latency_ms, status, purpose, key_type, conversation_id (FK, nullable), created_at 15. index_events → index_event.py: id, user_id (FK), document_id (FK, nullable), event_type, details (JSONB), created_at 16. system_health → system_health.py: id, metrics (JSONB), created_at 17. user_settings → user_settings.py: id, user_id (FK, unique), settings (JSONB), created_at, updated_at
All models must use the Base from base.py. Apply appropriate mixins. chunks.content_tsvector: Computed column `to_tsvector('english', content)`. chunks.embedding and memories.embedding: Vector(1536), nullable=True.

task.description:
Create the first Alembic migration with manual additions for RLS, pgvector, indexes, and seed data.
Run `alembic revision --autogenerate --message "initial_schema"` to generate the base migration, then manually add to the upgrade() function:
1. CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector; 2. ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; for all 14 RLS tables. 3. 14 RLS policies: - Content tables (documents, chunks, wikilinks): namespace='shared' OR user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::uuid - Private tables (conversations, messages, memories, dream_audit_log, projects, operation_log, llm_usage, index_events, user_settings, sessions): user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::uuid - api_keys: user_id IS NULL OR user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::uuid 4. HNSW indexes: chunks.embedding (vector_cosine_ops), memories.embedding (vector_cosine_ops) — CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS. 5. GIN index on chunks.content_tsvector. 6. system_config seed: INSERT INTO system_config (key, value) VALUES ('embedding', '{"model": "openai/text-embedding-3-small", "dimensions": 1536, "migration_status": "idle"}'), ('version', '"1.0.0"');
downgrade() must reverse all of the above in correct order (drop policies, disable RLS, drop extension).
Comment block at top of upgrade() explaining what it does and why (per spec).
task.verification: Migration file contains CREATE EXTENSION vector. All 14 ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY statements present. All 14 CREATE POLICY statements present with correct USING clauses. HNSW indexes for chunks.embedding and memories.embedding present. GIN index on content_tsvector present. system_config seed INSERT present. downgrade() drops policies, disables RLS, drops extension. `alembic upgrade head` succeeds against a running PostgreSQL.
task.done-condition: First migration creates all 17 tables, enables RLS on 14 tables with correct policies (content vs private vs api_key), creates HNSW and GIN indexes, seeds system_config, and installs pgvector extension. Migration is reversible.

decision.choice: Used SA Computed() for content_tsvector in the model but added vector column via raw ALTER TABLE in migration
decision.rationale: SA Computed() maps correctly to the generated column for ORM use. In the migration, the pgvector Vector type is not directly supported by op.create_table() Column spec, so the embedding column is first created as Text (placeholder) then immediately replaced via ALTER TABLE DROP/ADD COLUMN using raw SQL. This keeps the migration self-contained and avoids importing app models inside alembic/env.py.
decision.alternatives-considered: Import Vector from pgvector.sqlalchemy in migration (rejected: adds runtime import complexity and couples migration to app code); Use sa.Text for embedding everywhere (rejected: loses type metadata for future autogenerate).

decision.choice: Wrote migration manually (not autogenerate) — full explicit column definitions in upgrade()
decision.rationale: No live DB available at migration-generation time. Manual migration is also more resilient: autogenerate would miss the vector ALTER TABLE pattern, RLS policies, and GIN/HNSW indexes entirely. Manual approach gives precise control over all 17 tables.
decision.alternatives-considered: alembic revision --autogenerate (rejected: no live DB; would miss vector columns, RLS, and indexes).

decision.choice: HNSW CONCURRENTLY indexes use conn.execution_options(isolation_level="AUTOCOMMIT") before op.execute()
decision.rationale: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block. Setting AUTOCOMMIT on the connection before the HNSW index creation statements satisfies this constraint without splitting the migration into multiple files.
decision.alternatives-considered: Drop CONCURRENTLY keyword (rejected: CONCURRENTLY avoids table lock in production); Separate migration file for indexes (rejected: overcomplicates initial schema for no benefit).
